ELI5: What is this HAES stuff I keep hearing about?

The fact is that you CAN be healthy at any size, the problem lies in that every person is not part of the .0001% of individuals who could be obese and still have low cholesterol, blood pressure, etc.

And even then, they still are going to deal with a lower quality of life.

But the truth is that proponents of HAES are likely not the special part of the world that might be actually healthy. Instead it's the equivalent of someone trying to sell you on building a website by using Mark Cuban as proof.

HAES or healthy at every size promotes the idea that "good health can best be realized independent from considerations of size". In short size and health are unrelated. They often promote the idea that there is no way to correlate health to weight. So with only the information that there are two men of average height and one weighs 180lbs and the other weighs 600lbs, it is impossible to tell who is healthier.

Growing Up Post Original Trilogy Release

I was born in the 80's so I completely missed the original releases of Star Wars, nonetheless I grew up watching them constantly with my little brother and our parents because we all loved the films. Then, in the 90's came the announcement that 3 new films would be released and I was ecstatic, I would finally be able to see Star Wars in theaters! This was a game changer for us younger generations that missed the original trilogy in theaters, this brought so many more Star Wars lovers into the fold, and it really cemented a love for the franchise in those of us already familiar with the films. You must remember how amazing it was to see Star Wars in theaters back in the late 70's/early 80's, well these new films gave us that chance, and no matter how bad they were or how they will be remembered, I will always love them because they gave me an experience I never ever thought I would have in a million years: Star Wars on the Big Screen.

In between the second and third films we were lucky enough to have Tartakovsky's shorts Cartoon Network, which was again something very special for my generation as we grew up watching this guys' TV shows, and now he was blessing us with 5 minute shorts detailing the happenings in between episodes 2 and 3. This was eventually spun off into the TV series Star Wars: Clone Wars, which was totally awesome, and which helped us recover from the end of the new trilogy in a time when we thought there would be no more movies. My generation seemed to be pretty open to Star Wars moving completely into digital animation as we have been exposed to this style of animation since its' inception, and it seemed logical for a storyline in which some truly larger than life occurrences happen, meaning to expensive for movie production. We thought Star Wars would live on through TV series, and that seemed pretty cool. And then evil Disney bought the franchise...

Disney bought the franchise and people bitched, not really my generation but more so the purists, the people who saw Star Wars in theaters all those years ago; you guys bitched like you did when they announced Yoda would not be a puppet in Episode 3! And even though I love Star Wars and hate Disney, I was happy, because it meant a continuation of the franchise in movie form, which is the true form of Star Wars. They also produced Star Wars: Rebels, which was very OK, not good, not bad, just OK. I watched it a few days ago to see what it was about, and I didn't really find myself a fan. This series is basically Disney's attempt to sink their tendrils into children at a young age so that they are hooked on Disney's Star Wars, and not Lucas' Star Wars; or well, that is at least my thought on it.

All in all I am happy with the direction of the films and TV series, but I will really have to wait and see what these movies are like to know if I will continue to be happy...

As for the over commercialization of Star Wars, I don't live in The West, so I never see ads for Star Wars nor do I ever see such products for sale when I am out and about, thus it may be much different for me as compared to you; if I had to deal with the merchandising of Star Wars on a daily basis my opinion may in fact be much different.

You have an interesting perspective being younger and outside the US.

The first Star Wars (the real one from 1976) was nothing but a rip-off of old movie serials from the 1930s. It was really well done and different from all the other Sci-Fi available in the 70s. The next two films were slicker and a bit more self-conscious, but at their heart they were still rip-offs of old movie serials--complete action oriented escapist fare.

The only compelling reason to continue the franchise in any fashion was money. Lucas began marketing toys of every minor character from the original series, books were commissioned, "enhanced" re-issues on VHS were produced, PC games...all that nonsense began to overshadow the experience of the original films with their simple stories.

I guess the younger generation did feel excited to get a "new" Star Wars because they grew up surrounded by marketing that made it seem Star Wars was the greatest, most important thing ever. To me, however, all the rest of that shit just detracted from the original experience. The prequels were evidence to me that Star Wars just sucked because literally everything in the new movies was designed for marketing. The "story" in the prequels is absolute shit and is executed so poorly as to be insulting (I'll refer everyone to Red Letter Media's Plinkett critique on YouTube).

I'm sure the new Disney films will be critically acclaimed. I just don't give two-shits about it anymore. Not knocking anybody else, but I just think it's pathetic that people have bought into the whole "franchise" and "universe" mentality and basically completely quit supporting original movies. I'm sure Disney will be happy to give the masses their Avengers IX or Star Wars: Darth Vader's Resurrection--but I'll be passing. To me, Star Wars will always be Han Solo shooting first, Luke & Leia kissing, and aliens with latex heads.
